hook.en: At a public meeting, Gaitonde sees an empty chair on the stage. What he does next brings his adventure to an end.

objectives.en: Narrate the events at Azad Maidan
Explain how Gaitonde returns to his own world
Explain why he seeks Rajendra's help

narration.en: At a public meeting, Gaitonde sees an empty chair on the stage. What he does next brings his adventure to an end.

body.en: Gaitonde goes to a public meeting at Azad Maidan. On the stage he sees an empty chair meant for the meeting's president. Used to presiding over meetings in his own world, he walks up, sits in the chair and begins to speak. The audience is outraged by this breach of their custom and he is driven off the stage. This is his last memory of the other world.

points.en: An empty chair on the stage
Gaitonde sits in it and starts to speak
The angry audience drives him off

prompt.en: Put the events of The Adventure in order.

steps.en: Gaitonde finds himself in a Bombay where Indians are in charge
He notices the British are there only as traders
He reads history books at the Town Hall library
He learns the Marathas had won at Panipat
At Azad Maidan he sits in the empty president's chair
The angry audience drives him off the stage
He is back in his own world, after an accident with a truck
He visits Rajendra for a scientific explanation

explanation.en: The chair incident is his last memory of the other world; the explanation comes from Rajendra.

body.en: Gaitonde finds himself back in his own world. He learns that he had been in an accident, a collision with a truck, and had been unconscious. Shaken by the vivid memories of the other world, he goes to his friend Rajendra Deshpande to find a scientific explanation.

points.en: He returns to his own world
He had been in an accident with a truck
His memories are vivid and detailed
He seeks an explanation from Rajendra

problem.en: Why was Gaitonde driven off the stage at Azad Maidan?

steps.en: There was an empty chair on the stage meant for the president.
Gaitonde sat in it and began to speak, as he would at home.
The audience saw this as a breach of their custom and drove him away.

answer.en: Gaitonde, used to presiding over meetings, sat in the empty president's chair on the stage and began to speak. The audience was angered by this breach of their custom, and he was driven off the stage.
